descriptions.rankings: Every pack, pass, special and gift ranked by how much value it brings for its price. A ratio of 1.0 or more = worth buying at your weekly spend.
descriptions.spendRewards: Pick a cumulative spend-reward track and see up to which tier spending more still pays off.
descriptions.seasonalPasses: Pick a seasonal pass and see everything it gives, what the pass costs and whether its contents are worth the price.
descriptions.calendar: What runs when: the event schedule with a forecast for the coming weeks, and the packs on sale on fixed weekdays.
descriptions.events: Pick an event: which of its packs to buy at your weekly spend, what to buy with its coins (in unlock order) and whether spending more on it still pays off.
descriptions.sources: Pick an item and see every pack and shop offer that gives it, even nested in chests and supplies, ranked by what one unit costs.
descriptions.choices: Pick a choice chest, a package with options, or a group you can only buy one of (e.g. calendar packs) and see which is worth the most.

descriptions.compare: Pick two items with amounts: what each is worth, and the cheapest way to get it.
descriptions.gear: A squad's UR gear: in which order to craft it and to raise its levels and stars, step by step.

settings.heading: Valuation
settings.description: Settings that shape every value on every page, saved in this browser.
settings.countVipPoints: Count VIP points in the worth
settings.impact: Affects every value on every page
settings.vipOn: On: values follow the game's deal %, where VIP points are part of a pack's price.
settings.vipOff: Off (default): VIP points are worth nothing; each pack's other contents carry its price (coins, pickaxes and what they buy rise).

quality.heading: Model quality
quality.medianInfo: How far off a typical pack is from its deal % (0 % = exact). Higher with VIP points off, since the game's deal % counts them.
quality.withinInfo: How many packs the fitted worths reproduce to within {limit} of what their deal % says.
quality.holdOutInfo: The honest figure: the fit has {parameters} values for {packages} packs, so it matches them closely. Here the fit is redone without each pack in turn and measures how far off that pack then is, with nothing of it seen. The typical pack is this far off; the higher it is above the first figure, the less the worths can be trusted.
quality.uncertainInfo: Items the packs hardly pin down (they appear in few packs, or only alongside the same items). Their worths are the least reliable; the Items page marks them as uncertain.

schedule.lead: What runs this week, and what is likely coming in the next three. Forecasts repeat an entry's usual rhythm once it was recorded at least twice; a repeating pattern counts as running without being recorded, until no run was recorded for 8 weeks (two rounds for a slower one). Hover a bar for its dates and how long is left; click it (or its name) to open its plan. Dates and times are in your local time; a run starts and ends at the game's daily reset.
schedule.staleNote: No run recorded for 8 weeks (two rounds of a slower pattern): record its runs since then to trust the pattern again

events.heading: Event Shops
events.description: Pick a selected event (or the VIP Shop) to see its part of the best plan for your weekly spend: the event packs to buy, the coins they give, which shop offers to buy with them (in unlock order) and whether spending more on the event still pays off.
events.details: It's the same plan as on the Deal Ranking page, so both pages agree.

events.mineNote: Each pickaxe digs one tile; finding the floor's wish reward clears it. Unused pickaxes carry over to the next run, the floors don't: the plan only digs a run that reaches the last progress reward, and never past it (the floors above are listed for comparison). Pickaxes = per stretch of floors at the safety you chose above (up to the last progress reward; above it the average), cost = what they cost in the packs on sale (after your owned and free pickaxes), floor by floor from the bottom (the cheapest pack per pickaxe first, within its limits for the days left, whole pack prices), worth = one wish reward per floor (the best one for you), the other tiles' rewards found on the way and the progress reward for clearing the last floor (Details lists every reward).

sources.heading: Item Sources
sources.description: Pick an item to see every pack and shop offer on sale this week that gives it, including packs where it only comes nested (e.g. SR Resource Supplies → Herbs).
sources.details: Pick-one chests count as picking this item, random chests at their expected amount (~), generic items where they can be used. Per unit = Banknotes per unit, shown per 1,000 or 1,000,000 units for bulk items (shop offers at what their coins cost: bought from the cheapest packs on sale that give them, each as often as it can be bought per week, the whole pack price counted for the coins; coins no pack sells at what they are worth in your plan). Ratio = the whole source's worth ÷ price, as on the Deal Ranking (1.0 or more = a good deal at your weekly spend). Item share = how much of that worth is this item. Item ratio = worth of just this item ÷ price (≈ ratio × item share). Sources are ranked by item ratio, which is the same as cheapest per unit first. Rows highlighted green are in the best plan for your weekly spend.

gear.heading: Gear Upgrade Path
gear.description: The order to craft and upgrade a squad's UR gear (sword, armor, gauntlets, boots), one squad at a time.

help.aboutText: It tells you which gear upgrade to do next for your squad. Do the step in the game, tick it off here, and the page shows you the next one.
help.squadText: Choose your hero faction with the coloured buttons at the top. All three factions follow the same steps, only the heroes are different. Each faction keeps its own progress.
help.formationText: The squad stands in two rows: two tanks in front, the carries and the support behind them.
help.boardText: Next to each hero are its four gear pieces, always in the same place:
help.tileText: Each piece shows its level and its stars. A faded piece isn’t crafted yet.
help.nextText: A dashed frame shows what the next step will change, in the colour of its list:
help.craftText: First, every hero gets all four pieces: {count} pieces, one after the other. Craft the piece in the game, then click {done}.
help.craftAllText: Already crafted everything? {craftAll} ticks them all off at once.
help.craftUnlock: The upgrades unlock as soon as everything is crafted.
help.upgradesText: Now there are two cards, one above the other: the next level step and the next star step. Do either one. Each list keeps its own order.
help.levelText: Raise a piece’s level, up to Lv {max}. No blueprints needed.
help.starsText: Add stars to a piece. Uses {ur} for the first 4 stars and {mr} for the 5th.
help.blockedTitle: Why a step can be blocked
help.blockedIntro: Levels and stars need each other: a higher level needs more stars, and more stars need a higher level.
help.blockedText: A step that needs more stars or a higher level first is skipped for now: the card shows the next step you can do, and the skipped one comes back as soon as it can be done. If nothing in a list can be done yet, its card shows {blocked} under the buttons and says what it needs. Go on with the other list until then. For example:
help.holdText: Tick the switch on the star card. The steps to 5 ★ wait, everything else goes on. Untick it once you have {item}.
help.undoText: {undo} takes back the last step of that list. It’s greyed out while a later step depends on it, and crafting can’t be undone once you’ve started upgrading.
help.listText: Already further in the game? Open the full list under the cards and click the last step you have done: it and everything before it counts as done, everything after it as not done.
help.resetText: {startOver} clears the progress of the faction shown.
help.savedText: Your progress is saved in this browser only, for each faction separately.

lord.heading: Lord Specialty
lord.description: Plan your lord's specialty skills: the page tells you the level and extra Specialty Skill Points the build requires, how many of your points are left, and shares the build as a link.

how.points: Every Specialty level gives 1 point, and you can unlock extra Specialty Skill Points; each specialty skill level costs 1 point. A specialty skill unlocks at the level on the line next to it. Set your level and your extra Specialty Skill Points above the tree (saved in this browser): specialty skills above your level are grey and take no points. If you lower your level after spending points, those points are kept with a red count (right click removes them), so the build is back when you raise the level again. The bar below the tree shows the level the build requires (red while you can't have it yet) and your Specialty Points left; extra Specialty Skill Points are only mentioned once the season's levels don't give enough points.
how.clicks: Left click a specialty skill to add a point, right click to remove one; hover it to see what it does. On a phone, tap a specialty skill to add a point (it also shows its details) and hold it to remove one. With the keyboard, Enter adds a point and Delete removes one.
how.shapes: As in the game, the tree starts at Lv.1 at the bottom. Hexagons are active specialty skills (you use them in the game, then they cool down), squares are passive ones. The preview switch shows the specialty skills of later seasons (Lv.45/50), greyed out: they can't take points yet.
how.share: This browser remembers your lord, each lord's build, your level and your extra points. The page's address holds the lord and every specialty skill's points (not your level or extra points): Copy link copies it, and whoever opens it sees the same build. Opening a link shows its build; it replaces your saved one only once you change something.

lord.pickHint: Hover over a specialty skill to see what it does. Left click adds a point, right click removes one.
lord.copyFailed: Couldn't copy: copy the address bar instead.

items.heading: Item Priorities
items.description: How much each item matters to you.
items.details: "Don't care" counts it as worthless, "Low" at half, "High" at twice its usual worth. Only base items are listed: chests, supplies, choice chests and omni shards follow the items they contain (e.g. Antitoxin Level Supplies follow Antitoxin). A crafting chain is listed once, under its top item: Tempered Steel also sets Refined Iron, Brass, Leather and Cloth. Everything follows automatically, on every page.
items.exportHint: Download your item priorities as a file, to share them with others.
items.importHint: Load item priorities from someone's file. They replace yours.
items.importedSkipped: Imported {count} item priorities; {skipped} unknown items were skipped.
items.importFailed: This file doesn't contain item priorities.
items.footnote: Worth = Banknotes per unit at the weekly spend set on the Deal Ranking page. Uncertain = the game's deal % values barely determine the item (hover the info icon for why).
items.uncertainTitle: The packs barely determine this value (e.g. it only appears in one pack next to other unknown items).
items.explainUnknown: Unknown = there's nothing to base a worth on: the item isn't in any pack with a deal %, can't be derived from other items and has no recipe (or it's deliberately not modelled, like Moon Coins). It counts as 0 inside packs.
items.explainUncertain: A number with "uncertain" is the best estimate, but it rests on thin evidence: the packs barely tell it apart from other items, or it depends on a single pack. Hover the info icon for the reason. If it looks off to you, use Low or High to correct it.
items.derivedNote: made of other items; set those instead and reset this one to Normal

compare.heading: Compare Items
compare.details: You see what each is worth at your weekly spend, and the cheapest guaranteed way to get it within the chosen days (from today; weekly limits reset on Monday), including what else you get along the way.
compare.note: Random chests only count with what they guarantee.
